auditor_value: T = mg/√2; a_B = g/2 tangentially (vertically downward at B)

findings.note: The first equality drops the mass: equating the two tangential equations gives T/√2 = mg − T/√2 (forces), or T/(√2 m) = g − T/(√2 m) (accelerations). As printed, T/√2 = g − T/√2 is dimensionally false and would give T = g/√2, not the mg/√2 that follows it.

notes: Independent check: with zero velocities the inextensible chord gives (r_B − r_A)·(a_B − a_A) = 0, i.e. a_A = a_B; then T = mg/√2 and a_B = g/2, matching the solution.
